newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia 96/97 cotton exports to jump - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia 96/97 cotton exports to jump - ABARE.

text.p: The Australian cotton industry should achieve a record lint harvest in 1996/97, rising 35.6 percent to 571,000 tonnes from the 421,000 tonnes produced last year, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday.
The forecast, contained in ABARE's December quarter Commodities publication, was well above the 526,0000 tonnes forecast in the September quarter.
Australian cotton exports were forecast to rise over 45 percent by volume and more than 21 percent by value to A$924.0 million in 1996/97, ABARE said.

"Lower grain prices, bountiful irrigation water, good soil moisture levels and high returns for irrigated cotton relative to other crops are reflected in the 1996/97 record plantings of 388,000 hectares of cotton," the agency said.
"Current Australian forward contract prices for cotton, at around A$440/bale (500 lb), are A$95 per bale lower than the 1995/96 average," ABARE said.

ABARE said world cotton prices were forecast to fall by 13.1 percent in 1996/97 to average 75 U.S. cents per pound from 86 cents in 1995/96, with a related rise in world consumption to 19.0 million tonnes from 18.4 million tonnes in 1995/96.
